afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 290505
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
1005 PM MST Mon Sep 28 2026

.UPDATE...
Updated Aviation

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Bands of light to moderate rain with isolated thunderstorms 
will be likely over much of the region through Tuesday morning. 

- A Flood Watch has been issued for portions of the region 
Tuesday with a focus on south-central and eastern Arizona. 

- Below normal temperatures are expected through the week before
slightly above normal readings and much drier conditions spread into 
the region.
  
&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Tuesday/...  
The combination of tropical moisture from Hurricane Polo and an 
approaching Pacific low pressure system will continue to promote 
rounds of shower and thunderstorms through the next 24-30 hours or 
so. Through the remainder of today, bands of light to sometimes 
moderate rainfall will be present across portions of the region as 
enhanced southwesterly flow diverges from its typical dry status to 
provide the region with PWATs upwards of 175-250% of normal. 
However, the best mid and upper-level forcing and instability will 
be focused more over the westernmost portion of our forecast area, 
so most locations will see primarily a nice periodic light to 
moderate rain through at least this evening. 

The one exception to the lighter rainfall will be those 
aforementioned western areas (mainly locations around the Colorado 
River Valley), where heavier convection may be realized. There are 
signs that enough clearing will take place to allow some decent 
destabilization to take place, pushing MLCAPE values toward 500-750 
J/kg. With these areas also located under the best ascent due to 
their closer proximity to the deepening low, the environment will be 
favorable for the development of at least some isolated 
thunderstorms. Add in 0-6km shear of 50-60 kt and the potential for 
strong to even severe storms capable of damaging winds and even 
small hail will exist as well, though these should be very isolated 
at best. This heavier convection will also present the concern for 
flash flooding, as rain rates could reach upwards of over an inch an 
hour. Guidance points towards the best coverage of heavy rain being 
focused over La Paz County, and because of that, this area was added 
to the existing Flood Watch (in effect from this evening into the 
early overnight hours) last night. 

As the Pacific low continues its track southeastward into Tuesday, 
the more favorable environment to see further rainfall activity will 
begin to shift toward South-Central Arizona. As this progression 
occurs, shower and thunderstorms will begin to blossom over Maricopa 
and Pinal Counties soon after midnight. Activity will last through 
the remainder of the morning and into the afternoon, with the 
easternmost portions of our coverage area even seeing the rainfall 
window stretch into the evening. 0-6 km shear will continue to be 
quite impressive hovering around 50-60 kt, but even with a bit of 
low-level warm air and moisture advection leading to a slight 
increase in instability, the severe risk should be fairly low as any 
storms that initiate and can be maintained should only be isolated. 
Perhaps a low potential severe threat reaches into the afternoon if 
daytime heating can aid in further destabilization, but the areas 
that will see the best insolation during the warmest point in the 
day will likely be behind the best atmospheric support and moisture. 
By the this timeframe, any severe storm chances would likely be 
confined from around central Phoenix and eastward.

The main concern for Tuesday will be the potential for heavy rain 
and flash flooding. The greatest flooding threat will be for 
foothill and high terrain areas to the north and east of the Phoenix 
metro, where rain totals may reach upward of 1-2.5". The Flood Watch 
that was issued Saturday will go into effect late tonight, lasting 
through the evening timeframe. As for the lower deserts of Maricopa 
and Pinal Counties, the heavy rain signal has increased. HREF 
members have been consistent since yesterday indicating at least a 
30-50% chance of seeing greater than 1" within 25 miles of any point 
for these counties, while the ECMWF ensemble now has around 25% of 
its members showing upwards of 2" or greater at Sky Harbor Airport. 
Not to mention that EFI (Extreme Forecast Index), along with model 
shift-of-tails, a value indicating that anomalously high QPF values 
are showing up in numerous ensembles members, have been pulled back 
toward lower elevation areas. The preponderance of guidance led to 
an expansion of of the Flood Watch to include all of Maricopa and 
Pinal Counties.

There are some signs of lingering convective showers and 
thunderstorms behind the center of the low as warp-around moisture 
and insolation will help keep instability in place. Due to wake 
subsidence, anything that does pop will be reliant on enhanced 
terrain features providing orographic ascent. Hi-res data has been 
inconsistent on where it places this convection, but isolated cells 
may be seen as far west as La Paz County. By the time all this rain 
is said an done, most lower desert east of the Colorado River will 
anywhere from 0.5-1.50", while high terrain areas can expected 
closer to 1.50"-2.50". Locally higher amounts will be possible under 
heavier showers and storms. West of the Colorado River, rain totals 
will vary widely from a few hundredths in the driest spots to 
potentially greater than 1" if the previously mentioned strong 
convection is realized. 

The temperature forecast has taken a back seat to all this talk of 
rain, but for the fans of non-triple digit readings, you are in for 
a treat. Below-normal readings will be common across the region 
through today and tomorrow, with highs this afternoon ranging in the 
upper 70s to lower 90s, a good 10+ degrees below what is typical for 
late September, with much of the same expected for Tuesday. 

&&

.LONG TERM /WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
The low is forecast to move into New Mexico by Wednesday morning and 
well into the Plains by Thursday with dry air advection and 
subsidence increasing across our area. Generally clear skies are 
expected for the lower deserts on Wednesday and eventually over 
0808eastern Arizona by later the afternoon. Fairly strong ridging is 
then forecast to move into the region on Thursday with H5 heights 
quickly rising to between 586-590dm. Despite the quick boost in 
heights aloft, temperatures will be somewhat slow to recover, 
especially over the eastern half of Arizona. Highs should stay below 
90 degrees in the Phoenix area through Thursday with the lower 
deserts warming back into the mid to upper 90s. As the boundary 
layer gradually dries out going into the weekend, we are likely to 
return to our typically lower humidity levels while temperatures 
warm to slightly above normal. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0505Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:
Weather issues through Tuesday evening will include periods of 
SHRA/TSRA, lower CIGs, and erratic wind directions. A break 
impactful weather will likely persist for several hours beyond 
midnight, though cigs could locally flirt with 6K ft AGL. Confidence 
remains good that periods of SHRA/TSRA, lowering cigs, and periods 
of MVFR vsby will impact terminals in a 09-15Z time frame. MVFR vsby 
appears almost certain in moderate SHRA with cigs falling below 6K 
ft AGL. Brief instances of IFR vsby/MVFR cigs are possible around 
sunrise, however temporal and areal extent should be limited. 

Winds may become highly erratic in SHRA/TSRA overnight, potentially 
obtaining a prolonged period of a northerly direction, however 
directions should become E/NE as SHRA move east of terminals during 
the mid morning. Guidance suggests directions quickly shifting to 
westerly early Tuesday afternoon as 040-050 BKN decks develop with 
afternoon heating. After sunset, lower cigs will dissipate while 
winds weaken, then obtain the traditional nocturnal east component 
by midnight. 


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
The main weather issues will be SHRA/TSRA exiting the KBLH tonight, 
then gusty NW winds Tuesday. Confidence is good that winds will 
gradually veer to a W/NW component overnight, as scattered SHRA/TSRA 
move eastward into Arizona. Probability of direct impacts at KBLH 
are too low to include in this TAF, but brief heavy rain and lowered 
vsby are possible overnight. Confidence is excellent that winds will 
settle on a N/NW direction Tuesday with gusts 20-30kt developing in 
the afternoon. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Elevated moisture levels and periods of showers and thunderstorms 
are expected through Tuesday. The peak time frame for rainfall 
should be today over the western districts and tonight through 
Tuesday afternoon for the eastern districts. Chances for wetting 
rain between 40-80% should greatly limit any threat of dry lightning 
starts. Outside of enhanced gusts associated with stronger storms 
and some marginal northwesterly breeziness for the western districts 
Tuesday, winds will follow light and diurnal trends otherwise. Drier 
conditions and near to slightly above normal temperatures are 
forecast for later this week and through next weekend.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Flood Watch from midnight MST tonight through Tuesday evening 
     for AZZ534-537>563.

     Flood Watch through late tonight for AZZ533.

CA...None.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...RW
LONG TERM...Kuhlman 
AVIATION...18
FIRE WEATHER...Kuhlman
